paras: MSCI just finalized rules that make companies that mostly hold investments, rather than run a business, <g>ineligible for its global indexes.</g>
<u>In MSCI's own test run on May data, Strategy, Metaplanet and Yellow Cake were flagged for removal.</u>
Bitcoin treasury companies get no special treatment anymore: from the November review, they face the same test.

items.l: changes take effect at the close
ratios a company must fail to be out

paras: <g>Step 1:</g> does the company have real operating assets, tied to an actual business?
<g>Step 2:</g> if not, MSCI checks 5 ratios covering expenses, cash flow, asset-value swings and reliance on outside financing. <u>Fail 4 of 5 and you're ineligible.</u>
There's a buffer: a current member is only removed if it fails in <g>both</g> of its last two annual filings.

items.l: members must fail both annual filings

paras: JPMorgan estimates exclusion could force about <r>$2.8B</r> of index-fund selling in MSTR stock.
<u>That selling hits the shares, not Strategy's bitcoin.</u>
Saylor argues Strategy is an operating company with a software business and a bitcoin treasury, not a fund.
MSTR closed Thursday about <r>72% below</r> its November 2024 record.
